Freddie Mercury's own contemporaneous quoted statements on Queen's touring/recording routine

risk_tolerance.rationale: Performed Queen's 20-minute Live Aid set on July 13, 1985 against his own doctor's explicit advice not to perform, following pre-show vocal complications -- a specific, dated instance of prioritizing a commitment over direct medical caution, corroborated by named bandmate accounts.

decisiveness.rationale: In his own words, described wanting to break out of what he called a "rut" of the repetitive album-tour-album cycle -- a specific, self-articulated dissatisfaction that led to a deliberate change in how the band approached its work rather than continuing the established pattern by default.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Commanded the Live Aid Wembley crowd of roughly 72,000 (and a global television audience) through an extended, unaccompanied vocal call-and-response exchange, a specific, dated, widely-documented instance of live crowd command, independently corroborated by named bandmate accounts and contemporary press.

adaptability.rationale: His own stated dissatisfaction with the band's repetitive touring/recording cycle documents a specific, self-aware recognition of a pattern he wanted to change, reflected in the band's subsequent shift in approach.

provenance.notes: Roster33 (2026-09-16, docs/checkpoints/roster33.md): arts_culture priority pick (music), a second, genre-distinct musician alongside Bob Dylan this cycle. Wikidata QID verified live before scoring. 3 sources: Wikipedia (orientation), independent journalism and named-bandmate (Brian May) accounts of the 1985 Live Aid performance, and his own quoted contemporaneous remarks on the band's touring routine. 4 rows scored, deliberately conservative row count -- this cycle's research concentrated on the single, extremely well-documented Live Aid performance and did not attempt to substantiate additional rows from thinner secondhand anecdotes (e.g. an unsourced childhood piano-frustration story was found but not used, since no clear primary or named-witness source could be identified for it). His 1991 AIDS-related death and his private life were not used as evidence for any row, consistent with this project's health/private-life discipline.
